image_description: A low-angle shot of a traffic light suspended from a horizontal mast arm against an overcast, gray sky. The traffic light housing is black and vertical, displaying three circular lights: the top red light is illuminated, the middle amber light is illuminated, and the bottom green light is illuminated. To the right, there are silhouettes of street lamp poles and some distant building structures. On the left, dark tree foliage is visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The lenses are proportionally correct for a standard traffic signal, occupying the majority of the front face width.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Visor or hood extends over each lens to reduce glare.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The standard vertical arrangement is present. Note: All three lights appear to be illuminated simultaneously (Red, Amber, Green), which is functionally incorrect for real-world operation but structurally present as requested by the class definition.

artifact_observations.location: Top of the traffic light housing / Mast arm connection
artifact_observations.reasoning: There is a strange, thin, rectangular panel or fin-like structure extending vertically from the top of the traffic light housing where it meets the mast arm. This does not match standard mounting hardware and looks like a geometric hallucination or fusion of the pole and the light box.

All three lights (Red, Amber, Green) are illuminated simultaneously. While this is a 'visual' feature, it represents a logical artifact in the generation of a functional object, though strictly speaking, the geometry is intact.
The street lamps in the background have slightly inconsistent geometry; the curves of the arms look somewhat warped and lack clear mechanical joints, typical of AI background smearing.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of traffic signal and rule out misclassification as other street furniture.
To analyze the strange vertical fin/panel at the top of the housing to determine if it is a structural failure or a valid (but unusual) mounting bracket.
To ensure the housing is a single continuous object and check for edge bleeding into the sky, particularly around the visors.
To evaluate the lighting consistency (simultaneous red/green/amber) and general render quality of the background elements.

focus_areas: Structural integrity of the mounting point between the light housing and the mast arm.
Edge sharpness of the visors against the sky.
Logical consistency of the signal state (though primarily a visual audit).
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'fin' or extra plate on top of the traffic light. Is this a real-world solar shield/sensor mount, or an AI hallucination? Also, note that while Red+Green is physically impossible in normal operation, the prompt asks for structural evaluation; treat the simultaneous illumination as a minor semantic/logic defect rather than a structural one unless it causes visual bleeding.
